content: Please see here for another early prototype: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZSWSYrXJdg I'm starting to experiment with error message handling here as well. I wonder if The Integer Game is a good name for it. The next world would be more complete Parity World, then induction (where we switch momentarily to natural numbers), then conjunction/disjunction, etc, etc. I think this game would be a good prereq for the other games I've been experimenting with... Comments very welcome!

I'm also experimenting something with blockly.
I mainly try to see how to map blocks to lean tactic expressions, rather than developing new games though.

Very nice direction! We are thinking along the same lines while building Proofly, a visual, block-based learning support system for proofs.

A prototype is now available here: https://proofly.rub.de/

The backend of Proofly uses Lean for validating proofs by learners. We are currently working on extending the supported blocks and using Verbose Lean as the backing language.

I was playing with the system and I found that I couldn't enter a value in the text fields on safari:

Clicking on the textfield an indeterminate number of times, sometimes shows an onscreen keyboard, but one wrong click closes it.

I think the block-based editor concept is very worthwhile. With the controlled natural language approach I've seen students have trouble typing the correct phrase and it can cause them some frustration. I've been in touch with @Thomas Zeume and I like their direction a lot.

@Alex Kontorovich, am I correct in assuming you're looking at this more in the context of learning Lean specifically, rather than mathematical proof as a concept?

No, my vision is for students to learn the math only, not Lean. (But once they've been trained in this kind of thinking, it will be much easier for them to transition to actually learning Lean, should they choose to do so in the future)

In that case I would consider to have the language a bit further from Lean: While students can see through the differences between paper math and Lean, it can be a hinderance. I think this kind of interface is a prime opportunity to get best of both worlds (being close to paper language, while getting feedback driven by Lean).

This is also a bit more in line with the feedback, I think that is very much along the lines I think would be helpful to students.
Hi @Shreyas Srinivas , thanks for pointing this out! So far, we have only tested Proofly in Chrome and Firefox. It should also work in Safari now.

Thanks for sharing! Some quick thoughts based on the video:

  • At level 7 (Universal Instantiation), why do you drag a value h into the specialize block, only to replace it by 3? Could you just enter 3 directly?
    • Indeed, why is there an h in Values at all? If anything, I'd expect it to be filled with an x, since that's the variable name in the hypothesis.
  • For the calc blocks, I wonder if explicitly showing the latest LHS of the equation (instead of _) might be nice? We obviously don't want to type this in Lean, or even write it on paper in a math homework assignment, but since the game will give it to you for free, it could make the chain of equations clearer.

Thanks @Aayush Rajasekaran! The "yoga" with round vs square blocks is that square blocks are new names that the user is supposed to supply; so you can't drag anything round (already existing) into it. On the other hand, round holes are for things that already exist. So "specialize" is waiting for a round hole there, but "3" doesn't already exist. For such situations, I keep a "default" round block available, and that's what you saw being moved into place. For the longer calc blocks, I think you're right that the user does not need to see "_" on the LHS, it should just go straight to the "=" (just as one would continue a calculation in natural language); I'll make that change - thanks for the suggestion!
Okay, that makes sense. Maybe rename the default round block so it's not labeled h, since that's the most common hypothesis name?
Ah, but that h is in a square block - so they should learn early on to change the default name to something else! :)
